exposure: Timing of antimicrobial prophylaxis for cesarean section (before vs. after cord clamping)
outcome: Gut microbiome composition (in meconium, at one month, and 1 year of life)
Metabolic prediction (amino acid and nitrogen metabolism, 2'fucosyllactose utilization)
Abundance of specific bacterial genera (Staphylococcus, Cutibacterium, Corynebacterium, Streptophyta, Clostridium)
cohort: Forty term-born infants whose mothers underwent elective cesarean section were included in the study.
finding: Timing of antimicrobial prophylaxis for cesarean section is critical for early gut microbiome engraftment in term-born infants, but does not impact antimicrobial resistance emergence.
mod_finding: The timing of antimicrobial prophylaxis during cesarean section significantly influences the early gut microbiome development in term-born infants.
